title: Chốt và viết ra extension trust model (quyết định, không code)
one_line: Write one ADR that ratifies or overturns how oh-my-pi treats extension code that arrives with a cloned project — no code, no build, no test — because the trust posture has already shipped implicitly, and a posture nobody wrote down is one nobody can change without breaking every third-party author.
user_visible_effect: None on its own. This item ships a document. The visible effect is that a maintainer can now answer "does oh-my-pi prompt before running extension code from this repo?" from a file instead of from two code comments, and that a third-party extension author can read one place to learn the rules they are being held to. The ADR also names, assigns and dates the enforcement work item that M2 currently leaves unowned, so the deferral is visible rather than silent.

files_touched.change: The decision record itself. Required sections, in this order: (1) Status / Decider / Date; (2) 'What ships today' — facts only, each with a verified file:line, no judgement; (3) 'Threat model' — name the adversary and the asset concretely, not abstractly; (4) Options A / B / C, each with its real cost including what it breaks; (5) THE DECISION — one of A, B, or C, stated in one sentence, with rationale; (6) 'The three answers' — the acceptance questions restated as quotable declarative sentences, not as open questions; (7) 'Consequences' — what this unblocks, and the enforcement item carrying a NAME, an OWNER and a DATE; (8) Revisit triggers.
files_touched.note: Does not exist — confirmed. The repo has NO adr/, decisions/ or rfc/ directory anywhere (`find . -type d \( -name adr -o -name adrs -o -name decisions -o -name rfcs \) -not -path '*/node_modules/*'` returns nothing), and no existing decision-record document. Documentation convention is a flat kebab-case `docs/` at repo root (~50 files: extension-loading.md, extensions.md, marketplace.md, plugin-manager-installer-plumbing.md, config-usage.md, …). Placing the ADR at docs/extension-trust-model.md follows that existing convention rather than inventing a new directory. It sits directly beside docs/extension-loading.md, which is the document the shipped types.ts comment already cross-references.

files_touched.change: Add one short 'Trust' section stating the ratified posture for extension authors and linking to docs/extension-trust-model.md. This is the file an author actually opens, so it carries the short answer and the link, not the reasoning. Cover in three or four sentences: whether project-local extensions load unconditionally or are gated; what `isProjectTrusted()` returns and why; where the full decision and its revisit triggers live.
files_touched.note: File exists, 51 KB, and is the main extension authoring document. Verified silent on trust: `grep -c -iE 'isProjectTrusted|project trust|no trust' docs/extensions.md` returns 0. That silence is the reason the current posture exists only as two code comments that no third-party author will ever read.

files_touched.change: One line under the existing `## [Unreleased]` heading (confirmed at line 3) in the `### Added` section — no behaviour changes, so not 'Changed', and nothing breaks, so not 'Fixed'. Lead with what a reader can now find, e.g. 'Documented the extension trust model: project-local extensions [load unconditionally | are gated] and `isProjectTrusted()` [returns a real value | stays a compatibility stub returning true]'.
files_touched.note: File exists; `## [Unreleased]` is at line 3, per AGENTS.md's 'new entries always go under ## [Unreleased]'. CRITICAL: line 1057 is a RELEASED entry under `## [18.1.16] - 2026-09-09` (section header confirmed at line 1039) and is IMMUTABLE per AGENTS.md: 'Fixed legacy Pi extensions failing to load when calling `ctx.isProjectTrusted()` in an event handler; the extension context now exposes it (always `true`, since OMP applies no project-trust gating) (#7955)'. Do not edit it. Word the new entry so it reads as documentation of a ratified posture rather than as a contradiction of that released fix — if the decision overturns the no-gate posture, say so explicitly and link the issue, because that is a behaviour change the release note would otherwise appear to reverse.

steps.instruction: Establish the facts before forming an opinion. Read the two shipped comments that already state a posture — packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/types.ts:487-494 and :548-561 — and the two sites that implement it: packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/runner.ts:1264 and packages/coding-agent/src/session/agent-session.ts:7406. Write a 'What ships today' list of five plain statements, each with its file:line: (a) project-local inputs are discovered and loaded unconditionally; (b) the project root is `<cwd>/.omp`; (c) `isProjectTrusted()` exists on the extension context at two declaration sites; (d) both implementations are the literal `() => true`; (e) no prompt, allowlist or gate exists anywhere on the load path. Facts only in this section — do not let the argument leak in here.

Do the one piece of research the plan never did: trace the project-scope PLUGIN path, which is a strictly larger exposure than the `.omp/extensions` path the plan discusses. Read packages/coding-agent/src/discovery/helpers.ts:1271-1307 — the block headed 'Project-scoped OMP registry', commented 'Loaded from the nearest .omp/plugins/installed_plugins.json relative to cwd. Project entries take precedence over user entries for the same plugin ID', which builds `projectRoots` entries with `scope: "project"` and `path: entry.installPath`. Then read packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/plugins/loader.ts:19 (`scope: "user" | "project"`), :93-95 (per-root enumeration of `<root>/node_modules`), and :331 / :407 (`resolvePluginPaths(plugin, "extensions")` resolving the `omp.extensions` manifest key). Confirm the entry point in packages/coding-agent/src/discovery/helpers.ts:1013-1021 and :1025 (`resolveActiveProjectRegistryPath`: nearest ancestor containing `.omp/`, else the nearest `.git` as anchor). Then write the conclusion in one sentence: a cloned repository containing `.omp/plugins/installed_plugins.json` causes plugin extension modules to load as project-scope roots with no prompt, and project entries SHADOW the user's. This sentence is the strongest argument in the ADR; do not weaken it.

Write the threat-model section. Name the adversary and the asset concretely, because 'supply chain' is not a threat model. The adversary is whoever controls the repository you just cloned, or controls a plugin version pinned in that repository's lockfile. The asset is arbitrary code execution with your credentials and your shell, obtained by running `omp` inside a directory you were told was safe to open. State plainly what is ALREADY true: `ctx.exec` is declared on the extension context (types.ts:1492) and a loaded extension already has it, and suspend does not yet revoke provider credentials (that is WI-1 commit 2, wave 4). Do not soften this into a future-tense risk.

Write the three options with their REAL costs, not the plan's summary. (A) Per-directory prompt: cheapest in code — the API is pre-stubbed at exactly the right shape — but it is NOT free, and the ADR must say why: two implementation sites must change (runner.ts:1264, agent-session.ts:7406), two existing tests assert the current value and will go red (see test_files), and it contradicts a RELEASED changelog entry at CHANGELOG.md:1057, making it a user-visible behaviour change. Also note the blast radius is wider than extension modules: the types.ts:548-561 comment describes project trust as covering 'extensions, settings, skills, resources', so option A either gates more than this ADR is about or is internally inconsistent. (B) Origin-tier allowlist: no prompt, zero friction, and the supply-chain boundary lives in configuration — but it requires an explicit user-scope entry, which is friction that has to be paid in a different place. (C) Defer explicitly: legitimate, but only if the ADR then states what M2 does and does not claim, which is half the work.

MAKE THE DECISION. Write 'Option A', 'Option B' or 'Option C' in one sentence, and no other answer. If the answer is C, the very next paragraph must be the 'what M2 does and does not claim' statement, because a deferral that does not scope its own deferral is indistinguishable from having not decided. This is the step the whole risk register hangs on: the plan records that the API author has already made this decision publicly and invisibly, and that any later change is a breaking change for third-party authors who shipped against the seam.

Answer M2-OQ5 in one quotable declarative sentence about `ctx.exec`: is it inside the gate's scope, or is it deliberately outside on the reasoning that 'if it loaded, it is already trusted'? Either answer is acceptable; an absent answer is not, and the reason is that gating module load while leaving `ctx.exec` outside produces a document that LOOKS safe and is not. The plan calls this out twice — as rule R8 ('`ctx.exec` không được im lặng bỏ ngoài') and as the second acceptance question — and the plan's own acceptance gate for M2 fails when the ADR does not name this answer.

Answer the third acceptance question: does `isProjectTrusted()` become a real value, or does it stay a compatibility stub returning `true`? State it as a decision with a reason, and if it stays a stub, say explicitly that this is a DELIBERATE, DOCUMENTED posture rather than an unimplemented feature — because that is exactly the distinction the shipped comment at types.ts:548-561 already tries to make and that no external reader can currently see. Also state the consequence: if the answer is 'real value', the two tests in test_files are deleted or rewritten and the released changelog entry is superseded.

Write the consequences section and close the unowned-work hole. The plan states plainly that the ENFORCEMENT of whichever option is chosen is M–L, is outside M2, and — critically — that NO milestone in the entire programme owns it, including M3, and that the marketplace-opening decision is likewise unowned. Since step 2 establishes that a project-scope marketplace install path ALREADY ships, this unowned item is not hypothetical. Put a NAME, an OWNER and a DATE on the enforcement item in the ADR itself. Then add the 'Trust' section to docs/extensions.md, and add the one changelog line under `## [Unreleased]`. Do not commit unless asked.

test_contract: There is no test, and that is the correct instrument — AGENTS.md forbids placeholder tests, and a document-decision has no observable runtime contract. The contract is a THREE-QUESTION acceptance that a maintainer must be able to answer from the ADR's text alone, without asking the author: (1) Do project-local extensions load unconditionally, get gated, or not load at all? (2) Is `ctx.exec` gated separately, or deliberately outside the gate? (3) Does `isProjectTrusted()` become a real value, or stay a compatibility stub returning true? Any question the document cannot answer means the document is not finished. Two NEGATIVE contracts also hold and must not be violated: the ADR must not leave M2-OQ5 unanswered, and it must not leave the enforcement item without a NAME, an OWNER and a DATE. What a consumer sees if this regresses: the trust posture stays decided by whoever happened to write the extension API first, invisibly, until the posture has to change — at which point it is a breaking change for every third-party author who already shipped against that seam, and no document exists explaining what they were entitled to rely on.
test_files: packages/coding-agent/test/extension-context-project-trust.test.ts — EXISTING, not written by this item. Currently asserts `runner.createContext().isProjectTrusted()` is `true`. It is cited as a contract-by-inspection: if the ADR's third answer is 'real value', this test becomes red and MUST be rewritten in the same change. It cannot be run right now (see verification).

packages/coding-agent/test/issue-7955-extension-project-trusted.test.ts — EXISTING, not written by this item. Regression test for issue #7955: asserts `ctx.isProjectTrusted` is a function, returns `true`, and that the command context inherits it. Same treatment — a contract-by-inspection that constrains any decision to make `isProjectTrusted()` real.
verification:
Human review by ONE maintainer. This item has NO build and NO test gate, and the plan is right about why: nothing in the tree changes behaviour, so `bun run check:ts` is entirely unaffected and running it proves nothing whatsoever about this item. Do not present `bun run check:ts` as evidence for WI-0 — doing so is the fastest way to make a decision item look finished when it is not.

1. The maintainer opens docs/extension-trust-model.md and answers the three acceptance questions from the text alone, without asking the author. Any unanswered question fails the item.
2. `git diff --stat` shows exactly three files: docs/extension-trust-model.md (new), docs/extensions.md, packages/coding-agent/CHANGELOG.md. A diff that touches any `.ts` file means code was written, which the plan forbids: 'Cấm bắt đầu bằng code trước khi quyết định được viết.'
3. `git diff packages/coding-agent/CHANGELOG.md` shows the new line is under `## [Unreleased]` and that line 1057 (the released #7955 entry under `## [18.1.16]`) is untouched.
4. `grep -n 'ctx.exec\|ExecOptions' docs/extension-trust-model.md` returns a hit — the M2-OQ5 answer is present and greppable by a reviewer, not merely implied.
5. `grep -n -iE 'owner|due|target' docs/extension-trust-model.md` returns a hit for the unowned enforcement item.

ENVIRONMENT WARNING, verified first-hand: `bun test` is currently BLOCKED outright. Running `bun test test/extension-context-project-trust.test.ts` from packages/coding-agent reports '0 pass, 1 fail, 1 error' with 'Failed to load pi_natives native addon for darwin-arm64' — the addon binary packages/natives/native/pi_natives.darwin-arm64.node does not exist. This does not change WI-0 (which writes no test), but it means the two existing trust tests in test_files are cited as contracts-by-INSPECTION and must not be described as verified-green anywhere in the PR. Build the addon with `bun --cwd=packages/natives run build` before any later item that needs a real test run.
gate: DONE means all five of the following hold. (1) docs/extension-trust-model.md exists in the tree and names a decider and a date. (2) ONE maintainer reads it and answers the three acceptance questions from the text alone, without asking the author: do project-local extensions load unconditionally, get gated, or not load; is `ctx.exec` gated separately or deliberately outside; does `isProjectTrusted()` become a real value or stay a stub returning true. (3) The ADR's decision is one of the exact words A, B or C, and its answer to `ctx.exec` is present as a quotable sentence — a deferral scoped as 'neither, we do not have a posture' is NOT one of the three options and fails. (4) `git diff --stat` touches exactly three files and NO TypeScript file. (5) The enforcement item carries a NAME, an OWNER and a DATE, and the ADR names the already-shipped project-scope plugin path as an input the decision had to consider. This gate FAILS if: no ADR file is in the tree; the ADR does not answer the `ctx.exec` question; the decision is not one of the three literal options; any `.ts` file appears in the diff; or the enforcement item is still unassigned at M2 close.
blocks: WI-10 — canonical authoring surface. Blocked because M2-OQ2 changes what 'canonical' MEANS for a third-party author; building a public authoring surface on an unwritten trust posture freezes the wrong contract. Wave 1 orders WI-0 strictly before WI-10 for this reason.
WI-7 — registerMode mode registry. Blocked because the registry is built on top of the capability layer, and whether capabilities are extension-reachable depends on the trust answer.
WI-11 — per-extension state persistence. Blocked because a per-extension store must know what a per-extension trust level is before it can persist anything keyed to it.
WI-12 — MCP contribution architecture. Blocked because MCP servers contributed by an extension need an approval-parity answer, and approval parity is a function of the trust posture.

M2 acceptance item 9 (§11.3) — 'Hai ADR đã merge (WI-0, WI-10)'. The milestone cannot close with this ADR absent, and that acceptance item fails on any of: (a) no ADR file for WI-0 in the tree; (b) the ADR does not answer `ctx.exec`; (c) the M2-OQ2 answer is not literally YES / NO / DEFERRED.

M2 acceptance item 12 (§11.3) — the `outsider-extension` fixture, which is loaded through the real install path at BOTH project and user scope precisely because this trust answer is undecided, and which therefore must be green under whichever posture the ADR picks.
effort: S — half a day of design plus writing the ADR, which matches the plan's own 'S để quyết định' rating. That estimate holds only if the author resists expanding the document into an enforcement design; enforcement is explicitly M–L and explicitly outside M2. Add roughly two extra hours over the naive estimate for step 2, because tracing the project-scope plugin path is research the plan never did and the answer changes the urgency of the decision. Implementation cost, for planning only, is M–L depending on the option chosen — and it is outside M2 but NOT outside the programme: it is a mandatory prerequisite for any marketplace work, and M2-OQ7 binds whoever eventually does that work to the option this ADR selects.
risk: Deferral — and it is the comfortable failure the plan's own risk register predicted. The signature is a decision that the API author has already made publicly and invisibly: the extension API shipped with `isProjectTrusted: () => true` in two places plus a released changelog entry saying OMP applies no project-trust gating, and nobody ever sat down and chose that. It stays invisible until the posture has to change, at which point it is a breaking change for every third-party author who shipped against that seam. The second failure is a decision that names a trust level but skips the `ctx.exec` question: gate module load while leaving `ctx.exec` outside, and you have produced a document that looks safe and is not. A third, newly-identified failure mode specific to this tree: writing the ADR against ONLY the `.omp/extensions` path the plan discusses, and missing that a project-scope marketplace install path already ships and already loads plugin extension modules unconditionally with project entries shadowing user entries. An ADR that omits that path decides a question the running product has already answered by shipping.
open_questions: A, B, or C? This is the decision itself and it belongs to a human maintainer, not to this spec. Nothing downstream of WI-0 can be finalised until it is written down.
Is `ctx.exec` inside the gate's scope (M2-OQ5)? The ADR must answer this explicitly; 'it follows from the module decision' is not an answer.

Does the ADR RATIFY or OVERTURN the already-released no-gate posture? Ratifying is documentation. Overturning is a user-visible behaviour change that supersedes a released changelog entry (CHANGELOG.md:1057, under `## [18.1.16]`) — that is a much larger decision than the plan's 'S, half a day' implies, and it needs a changelog entry and an issue link, not just a doc.

Who owns enforcement, and by when? The plan states no milestone in the entire programme owns it, including M3. This ADR must attach a NAME, an OWNER and a DATE. Who is that person, and what is the date?

Should docs/extension-loading.md also get a trust section? The shipped comment at types.ts:548-561 sends readers to that file, and that file is currently completely silent on trust (`grep -i trust docs/extension-loading.md` returns nothing) — a live dangling pointer to a document that does not answer the question it is cited for.

Does the project-scope marketplace path (step 2) need to be brought INTO M2 rather than left to the unowned enforcement item? It is already shipped and already unguarded, so treating it as future work is a scheduling risk, not just an ownership risk.

plan_corrections.correction: The marketplace is not hypothetical. `/marketplace install [--force] [--scope user|project] name@marketplace` already exists (docs/marketplace.md:51) and `--scope project` writes the NEAREST PROJECT's `.omp/plugins/installed_plugins.json` (docs/marketplace.md:20-23). The registry path is resolved by `resolveActiveProjectRegistryPath` (discovery/helpers.ts:1025, walk order documented at :1013-1021: nearest ancestor containing `.omp/`, else the nearest `.git` as anchor). The loader then builds `projectRoots` with `scope: "project"` and `path: entry.installPath` (helpers.ts:1271-1307, the block commented 'Project entries take precedence over user entries for the same plugin ID'), and `extensibility/plugins/loader.ts` enumerates `<root>/node_modules` per root (loader.ts:93-95, scope type at :19) and resolves the `omp.extensions` manifest key via `resolvePluginPaths(plugin, "extensions")` (loader.ts:331, called at :407). Net effect: cloning a repository that contains `.omp/plugins/installed_plugins.json` runs that repo's plugin extension modules, with no prompt, and those project entries SHADOW the user's own installs. The plan's premise — that the marketplace is closed and could be held closed until a trust gate exists — is already false. This does not change WI-0's scope (still a document), but it must be an INPUT to the decision and it is the strongest argument against deferring.
